name: kern_semctl
prose: Precondition: td is the calling thread, semid, semnum and cmd are the semctl arguments, arg points to a union semun whose member matches cmd (buf for SEM_STAT/IPC_SET/IPC_STAT, array for GETALL/SETALL, val for SETVAL) and rval points to a register_t. The function is entered with no semaphore mutex held. Postcondition: it returns ENOSYS if sem_find_prison(td->td_ucred) is NULL. For SEM_STAT, semid is treated as an array index: it returns EINVAL (before taking any lock) if the index is outside 0..seminfo.semmni-1, and otherwise, under sema_mtx[semid], returns EINVAL if the slot is not SEM_ALLOC, the error from sem_prison_cansee, from ipcperm(IPC_R) or from the MAC check, or on success copies the semid_ds to arg->buf (setting sem_perm.key to IPC_PRIVATE when the caller's prison differs from the creator's), stores IXSEQ_TO_IPCID in *rval, unlocks and returns 0; SEM_STAT does not clear __sem_base. For every other cmd it first converts semid with IPCID_TO_IX and returns EINVAL if out of range, takes the global sem_mtx when cmd is IPC_RMID, then locks sema_mtx[semidx], runs the MAC check, and sets *rval = 0. Each command (except the default) then calls semvalid and ipcperm: IPC_RMID and IPC_SET need IPC_M, IPC_STAT and the GET* commands need IPC_R, SETVAL and SETALL need IPC_W, and any failure is returned. IPC_RMID calls sem_remove; IPC_SET copies uid, gid and the low nine mode bits from arg->buf and sets sem_ctime; IPC_STAT copies the semid_ds out (key IPC_PRIVATE for a foreign prison) and sets __sem_base to NULL; GETNCNT, GETPID, GETVAL and GETZCNT return EINVAL if semnum is outside 0..sem_nsems-1 and otherwise store semncnt, sempid, semval or semzcnt in *rval; GETALL drops the mutex around a malloc and the copyout of all semvals to arg->array and returns the copyout error; SETVAL returns EINVAL for a bad semnum and ERANGE if arg->val is negative or above seminfo.semvmx, otherwise stores it, clears the matching undo entries and calls wakeup; SETALL drops the mutex around a malloc and copyin of arg->array (returning the copyin error with nothing stored), then re-validates, and stores values in order, stopping with ERANGE at the first value above seminfo.semvmx (earlier values stay stored), after which it still clears all undo entries for the set and calls wakeup; any other cmd returns EINVAL. All paths after the lock was taken release sema_mtx[semidx] (and sem_mtx for IPC_RMID) and free the temporary array, if one was allocated, before returning.
note: Slice cut the head: the function is kern_semctl (sysv_sem.c:690-954), not sys_semctl; the slice also runs into sys_semget. All returns and the done2 label read (lines 690-954). Reviewer reasons were only mechanical (name not in slice); the old prose wrongly said 'the caller holds sema_mtxp locked', which is false: kern_semctl takes the locks itself (lines 725, 754-755).

name: ttydisc_rint
prose: Precondition: tp is a tty whose lock the caller holds (tty_assert_locked), c is the received character and flags carries the TRE_BREAK, TRE_FRAMING and TRE_PARITY error bits reported for it. Postcondition: tty_nin is incremented first. If a rint hook is installed (ttyhook_hashook) the function returns ttyhook_rint(tp, c, flags) and does nothing else. Otherwise, if TF_BYPASS is set it skips input processing and goes straight to the input-queue store. With error flags set: TRE_BREAK returns 0 under IGNBRK, flushes both queues, signals SIGINT to the process group and returns 0 under BRKINT, and otherwise stores the character (with a 0xff 0x00 prefix when PARMRK is set); TRE_FRAMING, or TRE_PARITY together with INPCK, returns 0 under IGNPAR and otherwise stores the character the same way. Without such an early exit it applies IXANY (clears TF_STOPPED and FLUSHO), ISTRIP, and TF_LITERAL (clears the flag and stores c quoted); then, under IEXTEN, VLNEXT echoes, sets TF_LITERAL and returns 0, while VDISCARD toggles FLUSHO (flushing output, echoing and possibly reprinting when it turns FLUSHO on) and then continues with the remaining processing rather than returning; under ISIG, VSTATUS (with ICANON and IEXTEN) sends SIGINFO and VINTR, VQUIT and VSUSP signal the process group (flushing unless NOFLSH, and echoing), all returning 0; under IXON, VSTOP and VSTART set or clear TF_STOPPED (or, for a repeated VSTOP, leave it) and return 0; CR is dropped (return 0) under IGNCR; and in canonical mode VERASE, VERASE2, VKILL and, with IEXTEN, VWERASE and VREPRINT edit the line and return 0. Any other character is written to the input queue with ttyinq_write_nofrag. If that write fails, the function queues a bell if IMAXBEL is set, returns 0 when no canonicalized bytes are queued, and otherwise calls tty_hiwat_in_block and returns -1 (the only -1 return). If the write succeeds it canonicalizes the queue (in raw mode, or in canonical mode for an unquoted newline, VEOL or VEOF), echoes the character and returns 0. The tty lock is neither released nor acquired.
note: Both earlier reviewer claims were right: write failure with no canonicalized data returns 0 (tty_ttydisc.c:1232-1233), and the ttyhook_rint early return (1022-1023) and VDISCARD falling through (1085-1095, no return) were missing from the old prose. Every return in lines 1012-1252 listed.

name: ktls_resync_ifnet
prose: Precondition: so is a socket whose receive sockbuf has sb_tls_info non-NULL, tls_len is the TLS record length and tls_rcd_num the record sequence number to hand to the NIC. Postcondition: it returns EINVAL without taking any lock if so->so_rcv.sb_tls_info->snd_tag is NULL or if sotoinpcb(so) is NULL. Otherwise it takes the inpcb read lock; if INP_DROPPED is set it releases that lock and returns ECONNRESET. Otherwise, still holding the inpcb read lock, it takes the receive sockbuf lock only while it fills the modify parameters (tls_hdr_tcp_sn = tp->rcv_nxt - sb_tlscc - tls_len, tls_rec_length = tls_len, tls_seq_number = tls_rcd_num), releases the sockbuf lock and then the inpcb lock, and returns the value of the driver's snd_tag_modify(mst, &params), which is called with neither lock held. No lock is held on return and no reference count is changed.
note: Reviewer claim (locks are not taken on every path) was right: lines 2497-2502 return before any lock, 2505-2508 take only the INP lock and release it, the sockbuf lock is taken only at 2514-2519. Returns: 2498, 2502, 2507, 2524.

name: sosend_generic_locked
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the socket's send I/O lock (SOCK_IO_SEND_ASSERT_LOCKED); exactly one of uio and top is non-NULL (top must be a valid mbuf chain when uio is NULL, and data supplied in an mbuf chain must be small enough to be sent in one piece); control is NULL or a valid mbuf chain; td may be NULL. Postcondition: ownership of top and control always passes to the function: whatever is not handed to the protocol's pr_send (or to ktls_enqueue) is freed before return, and after a pr_send call top and control are treated as consumed even when pr_send returns an error. It returns 0 once all of the data has been sent (uio fully consumed, or the whole top chain passed to pr_send, or with KERN_TLS in software mode queued via soref and ktls_enqueue), and otherwise a nonzero error: EINVAL if the length is negative, if MSG_EOR is used on a SOCK_STREAM socket (both before td->td_ru.ru_msgsnd is incremented), or with KERN_TLS if resid is 0 and the TLS session does not permit empty frames; EPIPE if SBS_CANTSENDMORE is set; the pending so_error, which is cleared; ENOTCONN if the socket is not connected and the protocol requires a connection without implied open (except when resid is 0 and control data is present), or if it is not connected, the protocol implies open and requires a connection, and no address was given; EDESTADDRREQ if it is not connected, needs no connection and no address was given; EMSGSIZE if an all-at-once send (atomic or mbuf chain) exceeds the send buffer high-water mark or the control length does; EWOULDBLOCK if there is too little space (space < resid + clen, and the send is atomic or space is below the low-water mark or below clen) and the socket or call is non-blocking; the error from sbwait if the sleep fails; EFAULT if m_uiotombuf returns NULL; or the error returned by pr_send. td->td_ru.ru_msgsnd is incremented once when td is non-NULL and the function gets past the two early EINVAL checks. With KERN_TLS, the reference taken by ktls_hold is released by ktls_free on every path after it is taken.
note: All three reviewer claims checked and right: the two early EINVAL gotos (uipc_socket.c:2368-2371) precede ru_msgsnd++ (2376-2377); ENOTCONN has the resid==0&&clen!=0 exception (2429-2435); EWOULDBLOCK depends on atomic/lowat/clen (2454-2461). Return paths: out label 2578-2587; pr_send at 2550.

name: aio_aqueue
prose: Precondition: td is the calling thread, ujob points to a userspace aiocb, lj is NULL or a valid aioliojob, type is the requested LIO_* operation or LIO_NOP, ops is a valid aiocb_ops vector, and the caller holds no AIO locks. Postcondition: if p_aioinfo is NULL and aio_init_aioinfo fails, the function stores that error in ujob via ops->store_error and returns it, without having stored the -1 status. Otherwise it stores status -1 and error 0 into ujob and then returns 0 or an error. It returns EAGAIN if the global or per-process queue limit is reached; the aio_copyin error; EINVAL for aio_nbytes above IOSIZE_MAX, an unsupported sigev_notify, an invalid signal number for SIGEV_SIGNAL or SIGEV_THREAD_ID, an opcode not allowed for LIO_NOP, an opcode unknown to the file-fetch switch, a sync opcode on a file without a vnode, a negative offset on a read or write whose file is not a character-device vnode, or kevent flags other than EV_CLEAR, EV_DISPATCH and EV_ONESHOT; the error of fget_write, fget_read or fget; EBADF for a path (O_PATH) file; the error of kqfd_register; or the error of the queueing step (aio_queue_file or fo_aio_queue; LIO_MLOCK schedules aio_process_mlock and counts as success). On every error return after the job was allocated the job is freed (its uio freed first if it is not the inline one), the credential reference, the file reference and the kqueue knote list entry are released as appropriate for how far it got, and ops->store_error(ujob, error) records the error in ujob. On success it returns 0 in two ways: for LIO_NOP it drops the file reference, frees the job and returns 0, leaving ujob with status -1 and error 0; otherwise it stores EINPROGRESS in ujob and in the job, gives the job a credential reference and the file reference, inserts it at the tail of ki->kaio_all, increments ki->kaio_count, lj->lioj_count (if lj is non-NULL) and num_queue_count, and either calls aio_bio_done_notify if the queue callback already marked the job finished or inserts it on ki->kaio_jobqueue.
note: Slice head cut off: the function is aio_aqueue (vfs_aio.c:1502-1739). Reviewer claim (status/error stores skipped when aio_init_aioinfo fails, line 1516-1518 jumps to err1 before 1523-1524) was right. err1..err4 cleanup read at 1726-1738.

name: cache_enter_time
prose: Precondition: cnp->cn_namelen is at most NAME_MAX (KASSERT), dvp is not doomed and its v_type is not VNON, and if vp is non-NULL it is not doomed and its v_type is not VNON (VNPASS checks); the name is exactly "." only when dvp == vp and every other name has dvp != vp (KASSERT); the caller holds no namecache locks; tsp and dtsp are NULL or point to valid timespecs. Postcondition: the function returns no value and, on every return, holds none of the bucket or vnode locks it took. It returns without inserting anything and without touching the cache if the name is exactly ".", if DEBUG_CACHE is compiled in and doingcache is false, or if cache_alloc returns NULL. For the name ".." it first calls cache_enter_dotdot_prep, which, if dvp->v_cache_dd is already set, zaps and frees an existing ISDOTDOT entry there and clears dvp->v_cache_dd, before the new entry is allocated. After allocation and locking, if an entry with the same name already exists (cache_ncp_find), or if the name is ".." and dvp->v_cache_dd has been set again by a concurrent lookup, the new entry is freed and nothing is inserted. Otherwise the new entry is inserted: for ".." dvp->v_cache_dd is set to it; for another name with vp non-NULL, any existing ISDOTDOT entry in vp->v_cache_dd is zapped (and freed after unlocking) and vp->v_cache_dd is set to the new entry; for a name other than ".." the entry is added to dvp->v_cache_src (holding dvp if the list was empty); it is added to vp->v_cache_dst if vp is non-NULL, otherwise it is marked NCF_WHITE when ISWHITEOUT is set and inserted into the negative cache; it is placed at the head of its hash chain and NCF_WIP is cleared before unlocking.
note: Both reviewer claims were right: the original precondition omitted vp doomed/type (vfs_cache.c:2512-2515), and for ".." cache_enter_dotdot_prep (2465-2491, called at 2536) already zaps and frees an old v_cache_dd entry, so the cache is not left unchanged. Early returns: 2527-2528, 2534, 2542-2543; out_unlock_free 2697-2700.

name: vfs_export
prose: Precondition: mp is a valid mount, argp points to a writable export_args, and do_exjail is true only when mp is in the mountlist; the caller's credentials (curthread) identify the prison pr. Postcondition: it returns EINVAL, before taking mnt_explock and without deleting the "export" option, if argp->ex_flags has neither MNT_DELEXPORT nor MNT_EXPORTED, or if MNT_EXPORTED is set and ex_numsecflavors is negative or at least MAXSECFLAVORS. Every other path takes mnt_explock exclusively, and on every one of them releases it, calls vfs_deleteopt for "export" on both mp->mnt_optnew and mp->mnt_opt, and returns. With MNT_DELEXPORT: ENOENT if mp->mnt_export is NULL; EXDEV if mp->mnt_exjail belongs to a different prison and the caller's prison is prison0, EPERM if it belongs to a different prison otherwise; else, after clearing the public export (vfs_setpublicfs(NULL, NULL, NULL) and MNT_EXPUBLIC) when set, it frees the address lists and the netexport, sets mp->mnt_export to NULL, clears mnt_exjail (dropping the credential and pr_exportcnt of the caller's prison if it was set) and clears MNT_EXPORTED and MNT_DEFEXPORTED. With MNT_EXPORTED (also after a delete in the same call): EPERM if mnt_exjail belongs to a different prison; if mnt_exjail is NULL and do_exjail is true, an existing netexport is emptied and zeroed and counts as new; if mp->mnt_export is NULL a zeroed netexport is allocated and counts as new; with MNT_EXPUBLIC, vfs_setpublicfs is called and its error is returned (a netexport that counted as new is then freed and mp->mnt_export set to NULL), after which it no longer counts as new, mnt_exjail is set (when do_exjail and unset) and MNT_EXPUBLIC set; ex_numsecflavors of 0 is changed in *argp to one flavor, AUTH_SYS; vfs_hang_addrlist is then called and its error returned (a netexport that still counts as new is freed and mp->mnt_export set to NULL, otherwise it is left in place, so state from the earlier steps such as MNT_EXPUBLIC and a delete in the same call remains); on success mnt_exjail is set when do_exjail and unset, MNT_EXPORTED is set and 0 is returned.
note: All reviewer claims right: early EINVAL returns skip vfs_deleteopt (vfs_export.c:310-316 vs 431-432); a pre-existing, reset netexport can be freed on vfs_setpublicfs failure (369-370, 386-389); after vfs_setpublicfs succeeds new_nep = false (392) so a vfs_hang_addrlist failure leaves nep in place (405-411). Slice 257-526 also contains vfs_free_addrlist_af, vfs_free_addrlist and vfs_exjail_delete; only vfs_export (302-434) is described.

name: vfs_lookup
prose: Precondition: ndp is a nameidata whose ni_startdir is the referenced starting directory vnode (it is consumed and set to NULLVP), whose ni_cnd describes the path (cn_nameptr does not begin with '/', ni_pathlen includes the terminating NUL) and whose cn_nameiop is LOOKUP, or CREATE, DELETE or RENAME together with LOCKPARENT or WANTPARENT; the caller is in a context where the namecache and VOP_LOOKUP may sleep. Postcondition: it returns 0 or an errno. On every error return ndp->ni_vp is NULL and the vnodes it held (the directory being searched, and ni_dvp on the paths that reach bad2) are released with vput or vrele. Errors: ENAMETOOLONG if a component exceeds NAME_MAX; EINVAL if the last component is "." or ".." for DELETE or RENAME; ENOTCAPABLE for capability-mode ".." violations; errors from nameicap_tracker_add, nameicap_check_dotdot and the MAC lookup check; ENOENT if a directory is doomed (including a forced unmount seen while walking up past a mount root), if a symlink vnode is doomed, if a trailing slash is used when a nonexistent target will not be a directory, or if the leaf is doomed after the lock upgrade; the VOP_LOOKUP error (other than the ENOENT union-mount retry, ERELOOKUP and EJUSTRETURN cases); EROFS for a create, rename or delete-like result on a read-only filesystem; EACCES for a symlink on a MNT_NOSYMFOLLOW mount; the vfs_lookup_cross_mount error; ENOTDIR if a trailing slash names a non-directory; EISDIR or ENOTDIR from the degenerate-name path (an empty name for a non-LOOKUP operation, or a non-directory). Success returns 0 in these ways: for an empty name with a directory it sets ni_vp to the directory (and ni_dvp to it with an extra reference when a parent is wanted); for an EJUSTRETURN create or rename result ni_vp is NULL and ni_dvp is the parent directory, unlocked unless LOCKPARENT is set; for a symlink that should be followed it sets ISSYMLINK, leaves ni_vp the symlink vnode locked regardless of LOCKLEAF, unlocks ni_dvp if it differs from ni_vp but does not release it; otherwise ni_vp is the final vnode (possibly the root of a filesystem mounted there), unlocked unless LOCKLEAF is set (and exclusively locked when needs_exclusive_leaf requires it), and ni_dvp is released if neither LOCKPARENT nor WANTPARENT is set (the field is not cleared) or unlocked if only WANTPARENT is set and it differs from ni_vp. When FAILIFEXISTS is set without ISSYMLINK and ni_vp is non-NULL, it instead returns vfs_lookup_failifexists(ndp), which releases both vnodes, clears ni_dvp and ni_vp, frees the path buffer and returns EEXIST. The function writes into the path buffer (trailing slashes are replaced with NULs and a temporary '/' sentinel is stored) and sets TRAILINGSLASH, ISDOTDOT, ISLASTCN and MAKEENTRY in cn_flags.
note: Slice 1323-1576 is the tail of vfs_lookup (vfs_lookup.c:1095-1563), not 'lookup'; head cut, so fixed under the real name. All three reviewer claims right: EJUSTRETURN gives ni_vp NULL (1382-1407); symlink path leaves ni_vp locked regardless of LOCKLEAF and unlocks ni_dvp whenever it differs from ni_vp (1435-1439) and never releases it (success at 1521-1549 has no release); WANTPARENT clear releases ni_dvp (1503-1508). Cross-mount and failifexists helpers read at 944-1053.

name: sys_mount
prose: Precondition: td is a valid thread and uap points to a readable struct mount_args whose type, path and data members are user-space pointers (type is read by copyinstr in this function; type and path are also read through the mount_argsu helper, and data is handed to the file system's vfs_cmount). Postcondition: the local copy of uap->flags has MNT_ROOTFS cleared (uap->flags itself is not modified). It returns the copyinstr error (for example EFAULT or ENAMETOOLONG) if uap->type cannot be copied into the MFSNAMELEN buffer; EINVAL if vfs_byname_kld finds no file system by that name (any error that call reports is ignored); EOPNOTSUPP, before any mntarg list is built, if the matching vfsconf has no vfs_cmount in the vfsops table selected by its VFCF_SBDRY flag; and otherwise whatever the selected vfs_cmount(ma, uap->data, flags) returns, called with a list holding fstype, fspath and the noro, nosuid and noexec booleans derived from the flags. The temporary fstype buffer is freed on every return after it is allocated, before the vfs_cmount call.
note: Reviewer claim (EOPNOTSUPP returns before the mntarg list is built) was right: vfs_mount.c:1098-1102 return precedes mount_argsu at 1104. Old prose said uap->flags had MNT_ROOTFS cleared; the code clears the local variable flags (1073, 1084).

name: vfs_domount_first
prose: Precondition: the caller holds vp exclusively locked with a reference, fsflags does not include MNT_UPDATE, *optlist is the option list for the new mount, and the caller holds a reference on vfsp (all three are asserted or assumed). Postcondition: it returns EPERM, after vput(vp) and vfs_unref_vfsconf(vfsp), if the caller is jailed and either the jail may not use this file system type or vp is the jail's root. It returns the first error from VOP_GETATTR, priv_check_cred (when the owner differs from the caller), vinvalbuf, the vnode-type checks (EINVAL for a file mount of a non-regular, non-directory vnode or a regular file with more than one link, ENOTDIR for a non-directory when file mounts are not allowed), vn_dir_check_empty (with MNT_EMPTYDIR) or EBUSY if VI_MOUNT is set or vp already has v_mountedhere, in each case after vput(vp) and vfs_unref_vfsconf(vfsp). Past that point it marks vp VI_MOUNT, unlocks it, allocates the mount and sets mp->mnt_optnew to *optlist. If VFS_MOUNT fails it returns that error; if VFS_MOUNT succeeds but VFS_STATFS or VFS_ROOT fails it attempts a rollback VFS_UNMOUNT (printing a message if that fails) and returns the STATFS or ROOT error; in these failure cases it unbusies the mount, clears mnt_vnodecovered, destroys the mount if the rollback unmount succeeded, clears VI_MOUNT, and calls vrele(vp) (vp is not locked at that point), leaving *optlist unchanged. On success it returns 0: the new file system's options replace mnt_opt, *optlist is set to NULL, VIRF_MOUNTPOINT and v_mountedhere are set on vp, the mount is appended to mountlist, vfs_event_signal, the vfs_mounted event handlers, mount_devctl_event and mountcheckdirs run, vp is unlocked (it is not released: the caller's reference stays as mp->mnt_vnodecovered), the root vnode newdp is unlocked and its reference released, a sync vnode is allocated unless the mount is read-only, and vfs_op_exit and vfs_unbusy are called.
note: Reviewer claims (rounds 1 and 2) right: success path has no vrele(vp) (vfs_mount.c:1296-1310) and vfs_mount_alloc stores vp in mnt_vnodecovered without taking a reference (line 691), so the caller's reference is transferred. Early failure uses vput (1143, 1180), later failure vrele (1242). Slice 1042-1312 starts inside sys_mount's neighbour; the function is 1118-1311.

name: vfs_domount_update
prose: Precondition: vp is exclusively locked and referenced, with VV_ROOT set if it is the root vnode of its file system mp = vp->v_mount; fsflags includes MNT_UPDATE; *optlist is the caller's option list; only_export and jail_export are the caller's export-option flags. Postcondition: on every return vp is unlocked and the caller's reference on it is released (vput on the early paths, vrele at the end). It returns EXDEV, if vp is not a file system root and *optlist has an "export" option, or EINVAL for the same case without one; EOPNOTSUPP if MNT_RELOAD is requested and the file system is not read-only; the vfs_suser error, unless jail_export is true, in which case the failure is waived and recorded; EBUSY if vfs_busy(mp, MBF_NOWAIT) fails or if VI_MOUNT is set or vp already has v_mountedhere (after vfs_unbusy in the second case). Otherwise it marks vp VI_MOUNT, unlocks it, enters vfs_op_enter, and then: EINVAL if a "fsid" option has the wrong length, ENOENT if it does not match mp->mnt_stat.f_fsid (a matching option is deleted), and EBUSY if MNTK_UNMOUNT is set; these paths leave the mount flags unchanged. Otherwise it merges the new mount flags (only MNT_UPDATE when the suser failure was waived), sets mp->mnt_optnew from *optlist merged with mnt_opt, calls VFS_MOUNT unless only_export is true, and, if that returned 0, processes an "export" option through vfs_export (old or new export_args layout, with EINVAL or a copyin error recorded as the export error). If VFS_MOUNT failed, the earlier flag bits are restored except that the current MNT_QUOTA bit is kept; if it succeeded, MNT_UPDATE, MNT_RELOAD, MNT_FORCE and MNT_SNAPSHOT are cleared and a pending MNT_UNION is applied; MNTK_ASYNC is recomputed either way. On VFS_MOUNT success it also sends a REMOUNT devctl event, replaces mnt_opt with the new options, sets *optlist to NULL, refreshes mnt_stat with VFS_STATFS (its result ignored) and allocates or deallocates the sync vnode according to MNT_RDONLY. The final return value is the VFS_MOUNT error if non-zero, otherwise the export error (0 if none).
note: All reviewer claims right: failure restores old flags except current MNT_QUOTA (vfs_mount.c:1554); vp is VOP_UNLOCKed at 1395 so later errors do not vput; the end label calls vrele(vp), not vput (1593), and the early returns use vput (1347, 1357, 1379, 1384, 1390). Return value at 1594.

name: __qdivrem
prose: Precondition: uq and vq are the dividend and divisor, and arq is NULL or points to a writable u_quad_t. Postcondition: if vq is 0 the function executes 1 / zero on a volatile zero, an integer division by zero, which the hardware or compiler may trap or treat as undefined; if execution continues it stores uq through arq when arq is non-NULL and returns the value built from the result. If uq < vq it stores uq through arq when arq is non-NULL and returns 0. Otherwise (vq != 0, uq >= vq) it divides using base-65536 digits, with a short-division path when the divisor has a single non-zero digit and Knuth's Algorithm D otherwise, returns the quotient uq / vq, and stores the remainder uq % vq through arq when arq is non-NULL. It reads and writes only its own locals and *arq.
note: Slice 253-273 is the tail of __qdivrem (libkern/qdivrem.c:80-273), the function whose head was cut; fixed under the real name. All returns read: 99, 104, 159, 272; the remainder is stored at 156, 267, 98, 103.

name: strrchr
prose: Precondition: cp points to a NUL-terminated string. Postcondition: the function scans bytes from cp up to and including the terminating NUL, comparing each byte, promoted to int, with ch as passed (ch is not converted to char first). It returns a pointer to the last scanned position whose byte equals ch, or NULL if no position matches. The terminating NUL is scanned, so when ch is 0 the address of the terminating NUL is returned (never NULL for a valid string). A ch that no byte value can equal after promotion, such as 256 or, on targets where char is unsigned, a negative value, finds no match and gives NULL; where char is signed, a negative ch matches a byte whose signed value equals it, and a ch in 128..255 matches nothing. The string is not modified; no locks or references are involved and ownership of the buffer stays with the caller.
note: All three reviewer claims right: the NUL is included because the *p == ch test (strrchr.c:42) precedes the *p == '\0' return (44-45); ch is compared as int, not converted to char, so ch=256 never matches the NUL and a negative ch can match on signed-char targets.

name: pow_w
prose: Precondition: w points to a struct wtab (normally from wtab_alloc), whose w_tab[i] holds approximately (1 - 1/weight)^(2^i) in fixed point with FP_SHIFT fractional bits and whose w_param_max is 0 or the power of two 1 << i for the first i >= 1 with w_tab[i] == 0. Postcondition: the function returns 0 if n >= w->w_param_max (this includes every n >= 0 when w_param_max is 0); otherwise it returns 1 << FP_SHIFT if n <= 0; otherwise, for 0 < n < w_param_max, it returns the fixed-point product over the set bits i of n of w->w_tab[i], computed as val = (val * w->w_tab[i]) >> FP_SHIFT starting from 1 << FP_SHIFT, in ascending bit order. It only reads *w, has no side effects and takes no locks.
note: Both reviewer claims right: with w_param_max == 0 and n == 0 the first test n >= w_param_max is true so 0 is returned, not 1<<FP_SHIFT (altq_red.c:607-608); with weight == 1, w_tab[0] = 0 (line 571) so w_param_max becomes 2 (574-575) while w_tab[0] is zero, contradicting 'nonzero for all j < i'. Returns: 608, 612, 624.

name: bpfioctl
prose: Precondition: dev, cmd, addr, flags and td are the ioctl arguments; addr points to a kernel copy of the argument structure whose layout depends on cmd (for example u_int for most BIOC* set and get commands, struct bpf_stat for BIOCGSTATS, struct bpf_program for BIOCSETF). The descriptor is obtained from the cdev private data. Postcondition: it returns the devfs_get_cdevpriv error if there is no descriptor. Otherwise it refreshes the descriptor's PID, stops the read timeout callout if the state was BPF_WAITING, and sets the state to BPF_IDLE; then, if the descriptor is locked (bd_locked == 1), it returns EPERM for every command that is not in a fixed list of read-only or harmless commands (BIOCGBLEN, BIOCFLUSH, BIOCGDLT, BIOCGETIF, BIOCGSTATS, BIOCVERSION, BIOCSTSTAMP, BIOCIMMEDIATE, BIOCLOCK, BIOCROTZBUF and others named in lines 1398-1424). It then dispatches on cmd: an unknown cmd gives EINVAL; FIONREAD returns the bytes held in the store and hold buffers; BIOCGBLEN, BIOCGDLT, BIOCGETIF, BIOCGSTATS, BIOCGRTIMEOUT, BIOCVERSION, BIOCGHDRCMPLT, BIOCGDIRECTION, BIOCGTSTAMP, BIOCGRSIG and BIOCGETBUFMODE copy the corresponding field out through addr (BIOCGDLT, BIOCGETIF and BIOCGDLTLIST return EINVAL if no interface is attached); BIOCSBLEN, BIOCSETF/BIOCSETFNR/BIOCSETWF, BIOCSETIF, BIOCSDLT, the zero-copy commands and the owner commands delegate to helper functions (bpf_ioctl_sblen, bpf_setf, bpf_setif, bpf_setdlt, bpf_ioctl_getzmax/setzbuf/rotzbuf, fsetown) and return their result; BIOCPROMISC returns EINVAL with no interface and otherwise the ifpromisc error, setting bd_promisc only when it was clear and the call succeeded; BIOCSRTIMEOUT returns the itimerfix error; BIOCSDIRECTION returns EINVAL for a value other than BPF_D_IN, BPF_D_INOUT or BPF_D_OUT; BIOCSTSTAMP returns EINVAL for an invalid value; BIOCSRSIG returns EINVAL for a signal number of NSIG or more; BIOCSETBUFMODE returns EINVAL for a mode other than BPF_BUFMODE_BUFFER (or BPF_BUFMODE_ZBUF while bpf_zerocopy_enable is set) and EBUSY if a buffer is allocated or an interface is attached; BIOCSETVLANPCP returns EINVAL if the value is above BPF_PRIO_MAX and otherwise stores it in bd_pcp without taking the descriptor lock; BIOCFLUSH, BIOCIMMEDIATE, BIOCSHDRCMPLT, BIOCFEEDBACK, BIOCLOCK and FIOASYNC change descriptor fields under the descriptor lock; FIONBIO does nothing; the function returns 0 for those that succeed. The vnet context is set and restored around the dispatch.
note: Slice 1519-1769 is the middle of bpfioctl (bpf.c:1376-1941); the old item name was a description, not a name, and the function exists, so it is fixed under the real name rather than dropped (rule 6). Returns and the CURVNET_RESTORE early returns at 1900 and 1908 read.

name: bpf_zerocopy_ioctl_rotzbuf
prose: Precondition: td is the calling thread, d is a BPF descriptor in zero-copy buffer mode and bz points to a writable struct bpf_zbuf. Postcondition: the function zeroes *bz, takes the descriptor lock, and, only if no held buffer exists (d->bd_hbuf == NULL) and the store buffer holds data (d->bd_slen != 0), rotates the store, hold and free buffers with ROTATE_BUFFERS (which also calls bpf_bufheld) and sets bz->bz_bufa to the new held buffer's user address and bz->bz_buflen to d->bd_hlen; otherwise bz stays all zeros. It releases the descriptor lock and returns 0; it has no other return statement.
note: No function named bpf_zerocopy_ioctl_getzbuf exists in bpf_zerocopy.c (grep); the old prose describes bpf_zerocopy_ioctl_rotzbuf (lines 504-520), whose head is cut by the slice (starts at 510), and the slice also includes bpf_zerocopy_ioctl_setzbuf. Fixed under the real name. The 'always returns 0' claim is true here: the only return is line 519.

name: bstp_transmit
prose: Precondition: the caller is in the network epoch (NET_EPOCH_ASSERT) and bs and bp are a valid bridge state and one of its ports. Postcondition: the function returns void. If bs->bs_running is 0 it returns at once with no change. Otherwise, if bp->bp_hello_timer.active is 0, it calls bstp_hello_timer_expiry(bs, bp) and returns without restarting the timer itself or clearing BSTP_PORT_NEWINFO. Otherwise, if bp->bp_txcount is greater than bs->bs_txholdcount it returns with no change. Otherwise it calls bstp_transmit_bpdu and clears bp->bp_tc_ack when bp->bp_protover is BSTP_PROTO_RSTP; for STP it calls bstp_transmit_bpdu and clears bp->bp_tc_ack if bp->bp_role is BSTP_ROLE_DESIGNATED, calls bstp_transmit_tcn (leaving bp_tc_ack unchanged) if the role is BSTP_ROLE_ROOT, and calls neither for any other role. In all of these last cases it then restarts the hello timer with bp->bp_desg_htime and clears BSTP_PORT_NEWINFO from bp->bp_flags. Whether a frame is actually sent depends on the callees (bstp_transmit_tcn returns without sending if the interface is not running or no mbuf can be allocated).
note: Slice 1-251 starts at the file head; the function is at bridgestp.c:153-191. Reviewer claim (STP non-designated/non-root ports send nothing but the timer restarts and NEWINFO clears) was right (lines 177-190).

name: debugnet_parse_ddb_cmd
prose: Precondition: this is called from a ddb command with the lexer positioned after the command name, cmd is the command name and result points to a writable struct debugnet_ddb_config; the options have the form -c <ip>, -g <ip>, -s <ip> and -i <ifname>, each separated by white space. Postcondition: *result is zeroed at entry, so any earlier contents are lost on every path. Each parsed IPv4 option is stored into dd_client, dd_gateway or dd_server as soon as it is parsed, so after a failure part of the result may hold addresses parsed before the error, while dd_has_client, dd_has_gateway and dd_ifp are only set on success. It returns 0, after the whole line was parsed to end-of-line, if a -s server was given; it then also records in result whether -c and -g were given and stores the interface found for -i (ifunit in vnet0, with no reference taken, NULL if -i was not given). It returns EINVAL, after printing a usage message and skipping to end of line with db_skip_to_eol, for a token that is not '-', a flag that is not an identifier, a flag longer than one character, an unknown flag or -h, a missing space after the flag, a missing interface name or a missing space after an option, or if no -s option was given; ENOENT, after skipping to end of line, if the interface named after -i does not exist; and the error from dn_parse_optarg_ipv4 (EINVAL for a missing number or dot, EDOM for an octet above 255), also after skipping to end of line, for a bad -c, -g or -s address.
note: Slice 1026-1125 is the tail of debugnet_parse_ddb_cmd (debugnet.c:978-1124); head cut; fixed under the real name. Old prose said result is left unmodified on failure: false, memset at line 1001 and the stores at 973-974 (*opt->result = htonl(tmp)) happen before the failing checks. Returns: 1114 (0), 1123 (error).

name: lacp_sm_rx_record_pdu
prose: Precondition: lp points to an initialized lacp_port with a valid lp_lsc, and du points to a readable LACPDU. Postcondition: the function returns void. It saves the old lp->lp_partner.lip_state, computes active as true if the actor's lip_state in du has LACP_STATE_ACTIVITY set, or if lp->lp_state and the partner field of du both have it set, and then overwrites lp->lp_partner with du->ldu_actor. If active is true and either the LACP_STATE_AGGREGATION bits of lp->lp_state and du->ldu_partner.lip_state are equal and lp->lp_actor matches du->ldu_partner in the bytes before lip_state (lacp_compare_peerinfo returns 0), or du->ldu_partner.lip_state has LACP_STATE_AGGREGATION clear, then LACP_STATE_SYNC is set in lp->lp_partner.lip_state if lp->lp_lsc->lsc_strict_mode is true, and otherwise left as copied from du->ldu_actor.lip_state; in every other case LACP_STATE_SYNC is cleared in lp->lp_partner.lip_state. It then clears LACP_STATE_DEFAULTED in lp->lp_state, debug-prints the old and new partner state if they differ, and calls lacp_sm_ptx_update_timeout(lp, oldpstate). No locks or references are acquired or released.
note: Reviewer claim (SYNC also set when the partner aggregation bit is zero; non-strict mode leaves it unchanged) was right: ieee8023ad_lacp.c:1730-1746. Function is at 1714-1759.

name: firewire_input
prose: Precondition: ifp is a firewire ifnet whose softc is a fw_com, m is an mbuf chain with a packet header holding the encapsulated packet (link-level header already stripped, M_BCAST/M_MCAST set as appropriate) and src is the sender identifier passed to the fragment reassembly. Postcondition: the function returns void and consumes m: it is either freed, handed to netisr_dispatch, or retained by the fragment reassembly queue. A frame shorter than a 32-bit encapsulation header only prints a message and processing continues. m is released by m_pullup if m_pullup(m, 4) fails (the function then returns), and likewise for the 8-byte pullup of a fragment. The first (and, for fragments, second) encapsulation word is byte-swapped in place. For a fragment, firewire_input_fragment is called; when it returns NULL (the fragment was queued or discarded there) the function returns, otherwise the reassembled packet has the 8-byte header stripped (a 4-byte header is stripped for an unfragmented packet). If m->m_pkthdr.rcvif is NULL it prints a message, increments IFCOUNTER_IERRORS, frees m and returns. Next, before any of the up/monitor checks, it applies the MAC label (when MAC is compiled in) and offers the packet to bpf peers if present; if IFF_MONITOR is set it frees m and returns; it then adds the packet length to IFCOUNTER_IBYTES; if IFF_UP is clear it frees m and returns; it adds one to IFCOUNTER_IMCASTS if M_BCAST or M_MCAST is set; and by EtherType it selects NETISR_IP, NETISR_ARP (after growing m_len and the packet length by ar_hln and copying ar_pln bytes from the position of the target hardware address to the position of the target protocol address, to leave an empty target hardware address slot) or NETISR_IPV6, while any other type frees m and returns. For the accepted types it sets the FIB number from ifp->if_fib and calls netisr_dispatch within the interface's vnet.
note: Reviewer claim (MAC tagging, bpf tap and IBYTES happen before the IFF_UP and EtherType checks) was right: if_fwsubr.c:580-609 vs 612-651; IMCASTS, however, is counted after the IFF_UP check (617-618). Old prose also wrongly said m is freed when firewire_input_fragment fails: it returns NULL for queued fragments too (551-553). Slice head was cut; function is at 516-657.

name: MPPC_Decompress
prose: Precondition: *src points to *srcCnt bytes of compressed (or uncompressed-flagged) input, *dst points to a writable output buffer of *dstCnt bytes, history points to a state initialized by MPPC_InitDecompressionHistory, and flags may include MPPC_RESTART_HISTORY. Postcondition: with MPPC_RESTART_HISTORY set the function first copies the upper half of the history to the lower half and resets the history pointer. It then decodes the input bit stream (literal bytes, and offset/length pairs copied from earlier history, byte by byte so overlapping copies repeat data) into the history buffer. It returns the status value 0 (that is, MPPC_OK cleared) and leaves *src, *dst, *srcCnt and *dstCnt unmodified if the history would exceed twice MPPE_HIST_LEN, if an offset code is invalid or an offset exceeds MPPE_HIST_LEN - 1, or if a length code is invalid; the history buffer and pointer may already have been advanced in these cases. Otherwise it applies protocol field compression: if the low bit of the first decoded byte is set it writes a zero byte at *dst and advances *dst, counting it in the output length (this write happens before the space check). If the output length fits in *dstCnt it copies the decoded bytes to *dst and the status is MPPC_OK; otherwise nothing more is copied and the status is MPPC_OK | MPPC_DEST_EXHAUSTED. In both of these cases it advances *src by *srcCnt, sets *srcCnt to 0, advances *dst by the output length and subtracts that length from *dstCnt (an unsigned subtraction, which wraps when the output did not fit), and returns the status.
note: Slice 260-282 is only the tail of MPPC_Decompress (mppcd.c:104-282): the old item mppc_decompress_uncompressed_tail is not a function, but its parent exists, so it is fixed under the real name (rule 6). MPPC_OK is 5, so rtn &= ~MPPC_OK yields 0 (mppc.h:46). Possible issue noticed, not claimed in the prose: bits is a uint32_t decremented without re-checking while multi-byte fields are read (lines 121-236).

name: pfil_head_register
prose: Precondition: pa points to a pfil_head_args whose pa_version is PFIL_VERSION (checked only by MPASS) and whose pa_headname is a NUL-terminated string that stays valid for the life of the head; the caller does not hold the pfil lock. Postcondition: the function allocates a pfil_head with M_WAITOK (so the allocation does not fail) and returns it; the head's head_flags and head_type are copied from pa, head_name is set to pa->pa_headname itself (the string is not copied), head_nhooksin and head_nhooksout are 0 and the in and out chains are empty. Under the pfil lock it compares the name with every head in the current vnet's V_pfil_head_list, printing a duplicate message for each match, and then inserts the new head at the front of that list regardless of duplicates, before releasing the lock.
note: Slice 258-510 starts mid-function; function is pfil.c:253-279. Old prose said head_name is copied and the list is global: head_name = pa->pa_headname stores the pointer (line 265) and the list is the per-VNET V_pfil_head_list (270, 275).

name: vegas_ack_received
prose: Precondition: ccv is the cc_var of a connection using the Vegas algorithm, ccv->cc_data points to an initialized struct vegas, ccv->tp is valid and the ERTT helper's OSD data exists for the connection (the result of khelp_get_osd is not checked for NULL); ack_type is the ACK signal. Postcondition: the function returns void. If ERTT_NEW_MEASUREMENT is set in the ERTT flags and both minrtt and markedpkt_rtt are nonzero, it computes ndiff = ((marked_snd_cwnd / minrtt) - (bytes_tx_in_marked_rtt / markedpkt_rtt)) * minrtt / mss and then: if ndiff < V_vegas_alpha, it flips slow_start_toggle when snd_cwnd <= snd_ssthresh, and otherwise sets slow_start_toggle to 0 and snd_cwnd to min(snd_cwnd + mss, TCP_MAXWIN << snd_scale); if ndiff > V_vegas_beta, it calls vegas_cong_signal(ccv, CC_VEGAS_RATE) and then sets slow_start_toggle to 0; if ndiff is between alpha and beta inclusive, neither the window nor the toggle is changed. When ERTT_NEW_MEASUREMENT was set it is cleared whether or not the measurement was used. Finally, if slow_start_toggle is nonzero it calls newreno_cc_ack_received(ccv, ack_type), which can also increase snd_cwnd. No locks or references are acquired or released by this function.
note: Reviewer claim (code leaves snd_cwnd unchanged when alpha <= ndiff <= beta, and omits the newreno fallback) was right: cc_vegas.c:145-161 and 166-167. Function at 126-168.

name: vegas_data_sz
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: the function returns sizeof(struct vegas), the size in bytes of the per-connection Vegas state, which has a single int member (slow_start_toggle); it has no side effects and acquires no locks or references.
contract: /*@ requires true; ensures result == sizeof(struct vegas); */
note: Function at cc_vegas.c:176-180; a single return. The old contract result == 4 depended on the size of int; replaced with sizeof(struct vegas). Reviewer claim (old prose said it returns 0 and sets a result) was right.

name: bsearch4_process_record
prose: Precondition: dst_array, stack and rib_entry point to initialized bsearch4_array and bsearch4_record objects (arr arrays allocated for alloc_items entries, the stack for 32), the records are in host byte order, and rib_entry comes from a list sorted by rr_cmp (by address, then by mask value ascending, so a less specific prefix comes before a more specific prefix with the same address); the in-code comment says the stack always bottoms out at 0.0.0.0/0. Postcondition: the function returns true unless dst_array is full when a record has to be appended, in which case it returns false (the only false returns come from add_array_entry on dst_array). It first pops stack entries that do not contain rib_entry (pst->addr4 != (rib_entry->addr4 & pst->mask4)), each pop decrementing stack->num_items and possibly appending a record to dst_array through pop_stack_entry. If dst_array is not empty it then, when there is a gap between the last address covered by the last dst_array record and rib_entry->addr4, appends a record with the top stack entry's mask and next hop covering the gap. If the last dst_array record has the same address as rib_entry it replaces that record with *rib_entry, pushes rib_entry on the stack (the push result is ignored) and returns true. Otherwise it appends rib_entry to dst_array, pushes it on the stack (result ignored, so a full stack is silently not extended) and returns true. For the very first record (both arrays empty) it just appends and pushes.
note: Both reviewer claims right: the stack is empty on the first call (so 'contains 0.0.0.0/0' is not a precondition of the first call), and the order required is less specific first (rr_cmp, in_fib_algo.c:221-242) even though the comment at 327 says 'larger prefixes'. Function at 312-381; false returns at 334, 360, 377.

name: DXR_LOOKUP_DEFINE(D)
prose: Macro-generated functions: DXR_LOOKUP_DEFINE(D) defines two static functions for the direct-table width D (instantiated for 15 down to 9, and for 16 when DXR_TRIE_BITS > 16). Generated function dxr_lookup_D(dxr, dst): dxr points to an initialized dxr and dst is a 32-bit host-order address; it indexes the direct table dxr->d (uint16_t entries) with dst >> (32 - D), combines that with the DXR_TRIE_BITS - D bits of dst starting at bit DXR_RANGE_SHIFT to select a direct_entry in dxr->x, and returns de.base if the entry's fragments equal FRAGS_MARK_HIT, and otherwise the value returned by range_lookup(dxr->r, de, dst); it takes no locks and allocates nothing. Generated function dxr_fib_lookup_D(algo_data, key, scopeid): it converts key.addr4.s_addr with ntohl, calls dxr_lookup_D on algo_data (a struct dxr) and returns the element of dxr->nh_tbl at the index that call returned, without checking the index; scopeid is unused.
note: The item is the macro (in_fib_dxr.c:291-315), not a function named dxr_lookup_D. Reviewer claim (macro also defines dxr_fib_lookup_##D returning nhop from dxr->nh_tbl) was right. Instantiations at 317-326.

name: INPCBSTORAGE_DEFINE(prot, ppcb, lname, zname, iname, hname)
prose: Macro-generated function: INPCBSTORAGE_DEFINE defines the static function prot_inpcb_init(void *mem, int size, int flags) (with size and flags unused) as the UMA zone initializer for the protocol's inpcb storage. Precondition: mem points to a zone item that begins with a struct inpcb (the zone item size is ips_size, sizeof(struct ppcb)). Postcondition: it initializes mem's inp_lock with rw_init_flags using the name lname and the flags RW_RECURSE | RW_DUPOK, and returns 0; it has no other return. The macro also defines the static struct inpcbstorage named prot (with ips_size = sizeof(struct ppcb), ips_pcbinit = prot_inpcb_init and the zone, info-lock and hash-lock names) and registers SYSINIT and SYSUNINIT hooks that call in_pcbstorage_init and in_pcbstorage_destroy.
note: The item is the macro (in_pcb.h:424-443). Reviewer claim (item size is sizeof(struct ppcb), not sizeof(struct inpcb)) was right: line 434.

name: vrrp_input_c
prose: Precondition: the caller is in the network epoch; m is an mbuf with a VRRPv3 header at offset off (vrrp_version == CARP_VERSION_VRRPv3, asserted by MPASS), af is the address family, ttl the packet's TTL or hop limit, len the VRRP length and phdrcksum the pseudo-header checksum. Postcondition: the function returns void and frees m exactly once on every path. It calls carp_find_ifa with the VRID; if that finds no matching ifaddr (or a looped packet) it has already incremented carps_badvhid or carps_badif, and the function frees m and returns with no softc state changed. Otherwise it takes the softc lock, releases the ifaddr reference taken by carp_find_ifa (once, before any other check), and then: if the softc version is not VRRPv3 it increments carps_badver; if ttl is not CARP_DFLTTL it increments carps_badttl; if vrrp_checksum_verify fails it increments carps_badsum; if the local priority sc_vrrp_prio is 255 it drops the packet without incrementing a counter; in each of these cases no softc state is changed. Otherwise it sets sc_vrrp_master_inter from the header's max advertisement interval and acts on sc_state: nothing in INIT; in MASTER, if the peer's interval is smaller than sc_vrrp_adv_inter or its priority is higher than sc_vrrp_prio, it stops the advertisement callout, moves to BACKUP, calls carp_setrun(sc, 0) and carp_delroute; in BACKUP, if V_carp_preempt is set and the peer's interval is larger than sc_vrrp_adv_inter or its priority lower, it calls carp_master_down_locked, and otherwise carp_setrun(sc, af). It then releases the softc lock.
note: All three reviewer claims right: priority 255 drops with no counter and skips the interval and state update (ip_carp.c:993-997); a missing ifaddr is not silent, carp_find_ifa increments carps_badvhid or carps_badif (808-816). Function at 943-1044.
